quote.text: Reality is that which, when you stop believing in it, doesn't go away.
quote.author: Philip K. Dick, How to Build a Universe That Doesn't Fall Apart Two Days Later (1978)

stories.headline: A Month's Quiet Ends Over the Strait, in a Single Night
stories.dek: American forces struck an island Iran uses to reach the Strait of Hormuz — the first exchange since July. Tehran answered with missiles at bases in Jordan and, it claimed, the UAE. Abu Dhabi called the claim on itself "baseless." Brent jumped past ninety dollars.

stories.headline: Nvidia Prints Ninety-Six Billion — as Its Biggest Customer Builds a Rival
stories.dek: A record quarter, ninety-two per cent of it data-centre, lands the same week the die detail arrives on the inference chip OpenAI and Broadcom built to bench against it. The margin, and the clearest attempt on it, in one news cycle.

stories.kicker: The Long Read · The Undercurrent — Indonesia
stories.headline: The Crowd That Rarely Buys
stories.dek: Walk into a Jakarta mall on a Saturday and it looks like a boom. Look for the shopping bags and there aren't any. Indonesia has invented a comic vocabulary for the gap between the two — and it has become the country's most trusted economic indicator, precisely because no ministry issued it.

stories.headline: The State Reaches for the Off Switch on Autoplay
stories.dek: Josephine Teo has set out the next step: a real minimum age of 13 on six named platforms, autoplay and infinite scroll off by default for teenagers, and a daily time limit parents can set. Legislation comes in 2027. The hard part is the one word nobody can yet verify — the age.

stories.headline: Everything That Matters Is at the Cut Edge
stories.dek: A belt is the easiest luxury object to judge cold, because the whole truth is visible at the buckle end and the trimmed edge. Learn four things and you will out-read the shop — and find that the last hundred and fifty dollars buys fit, not years.

stories.headline: A Quant Built for the Exact Chip on Your Desk
stories.dek: NVFP4 — Nvidia's Blackwell-native four-bit float — is the first quantisation aimed at the RTX 5090's own silicon rather than a lowest common denominator. It is early, single-sourced, and pointed in the right direction. Plus the Qwen4 preview from No.85, now running by expert-offload.

stories.headline: The Ring That Lasts a Fortnight and Asks for Nothing
stories.dek: The Ultrahuman Ring Pro ships with a two-week battery, no subscription and full waterproofing — the buy-once answer to a category built on monthly fees. And the camera-free glasses this desk flagged in No.87 finally go on sale this week.

stories.headline: Two Kinds of Driver in One Ear Cup
stories.dek: Noble Audio's first wireless flagship runs a dynamic and a planar-magnetic driver together — the sort of thing that used to mean a cable and a headphone amp. It is the news hook in an autumn the hi-fi desk got loud, and a reminder that "endgame" is a word to measure, not to trust.

stories.headline: The Lido Raises Its Curtain on Murdoch
stories.dek: The 83rd Venice Film Festival opens with Danny Boyle's Ink — Guy Pearce as Rupert Murdoch. The lineup reads thin on paper and thinner on women; the verdict waits on the McDonagh and Lee Chang-dong premieres, not opening night.

stories.kicker: The Family Desk · Screens & the Law
stories.headline: The Phone Leaves the Classroom. Now the Law Comes for the Feed.
stories.dek: For a twelve-year-old in Secondary 1, the rules are arriving from two directions at once — a school-day device ban already in force, and an age law taking shape for the feed at home. The evidence says the evening, not the classroom, is where a parent's work now lives.

stories.headline: A New Chair Says It Isn't Beaten — and the Anti-Fiat Trade Takes the Hit
stories.dek: Kevin Warsh used Jackson Hole to warn that inflation isn't done. The market flipped from pricing a September cut to weighing a hike — and then Hormuz put oil past ninety. Gold and bitcoin fell together; the dollar firmed. The whole week is in that one broken pairing.

stories.kicker: The Rabbit Hole · Vinyl Records & Turntables
stories.headline: The Needle, the Ritual, and an Eighteen-Year Climb
stories.dek: A format the industry buried came back and kept coming — eighteen straight years of growth, and forty-four million LPs against thirty-three million CDs. The hook is rarely fidelity. It is the sleeve in your hands, the one album you chose, and a chain where every link is a knob you can turn.

stories.headline: The Weighted Walk the Longevity Crowd Calls the Foundation
stories.dek: Rucking — walking under a loaded pack — is 2026's fitness trend because it holds the heart in the aerobic zone while loading bone and posture a plain walk can't. The number underneath it is VO2 max. And a former pro's rebuttal: they just rediscovered Tuesday.

stories.headline: An October That Opens with a Sprint
stories.dek: The season's marquee is a Grand Prix that adds a Sprint for the first time; around it, a Zimmer night, a stacked concert calendar, and a sumo basho to plan the flights around.
